description: Free, counts only. How two sets of places sit together: the share of set a within radius_miles of set b and of b within radius_miles of a, how many places overlap, and the county / zip / state / metro areas that have both, only a, or only b (top 10 of each named). Each set is a dataset, datasets or category plus filters, the same as count_locations; any US brand or kind of place works, including Overture lists from search_datasets. Example: {"a": {"dataset": "<slug>"}, "b": {"dataset": "<other slug>"}, "radius_miles": 1, "by": "county"}.

a.description: First set: dataset, datasets or category, plus filters

area_columns.description: Census, NOAA, FEMA and USDA facts added to EVERY ROW as columns named <kind>_<attribute>, each as "<kind>:<attribute>,<attribute>", e.g. "county:population,median_household_income" — the county / ZIP / metro / state figures beside each location, in the preview and in the file you buy, after the area's id and name (county_fips, county_name; zip_code; metro_cbsa, metro_name; state_code, state_name). Free. The same attribute words area_where takes (listed there).

area_where.description: Only rows whose county/zip/state/metro meets a Census condition, each as "<kind>:<attribute><op><value>" (ops > >= < <= =; values accept 1M, 250k, $50,000, 10%), e.g. "county:population>1000000". Every clause must hold; the fact is the area's, not the row's, and it adds nothing to the price. Attributes: e.g. population, households, median_household_income, median_age, pct_65_plus, housing_units; Census ACS people, income, education and housing; businesses and jobs by NAICS sector (<sector>_establishments, <sector>_employees) or detailed code (naics_<code>_establishments / _employees / _payroll); population growth; NOAA climate normals and actuals; NOAA storm events; station weather normals; hourly weather normals; building stock; Zillow home values; Zillow rents; building permits; IRS tax returns; FEMA hazard risk; USDA farm census. Every key (11,012) with its label, unit and kinds: GET /area-attributes.json.

areas_in.description: Only rows in these areas, e.g. {"by": "county", "ids": ["51760"]} for Richmond city, VA — the ids count_by_area returns, placed the same way (/find: areas_in=county:51760).

ids.description: County FIPS, 5-digit ZIP, CBSA code or state code — the `id` of a count_by_area row

exclude.description: Dataset slugs left out wherever the set expands: a category minus one of its members (a list's competitors are its own category with itself excluded).

metro.description: Only rows in one metro area (CBSA): its 5-digit code ("37980") or its name ("Philadelphia", "Philadelphia, PA"). The same as areas_in {"by": "metro", "ids": [code]}.

near.description: Distance search on lists with coordinates: ONE of place, zip, lat+lng or points, with radius_miles.

place.description: City or town with state, e.g. "Topeka, KS"

points.description: Several points instead of one place/zip/lat+lng (at most 10): a row counts when it is within the radius of ANY of them, e.g. an operator's offices.

radius_miles.description: Only rows within this straight-line distance of the point (or of any of the points). Free.

opendata.description: INSTEAD of dataset / datasets / category: a public register read LIVE from its publisher at question time (e.g. a state's licensed child-care programs). Matched by distance only (relate.mode near / not_near, near_m metres). Not a list we sell: the answer names the publisher, licence and read time, and prices only the rows of OUR lists.

source.description: The register's key, "<domain>/<id>" — search_datasets with kind "register" finds it, e.g. "data.ny.gov/cb42-qumz" (New York's licensed child-care programs)

state.description: Cut the register to one state, e.g. "NY" (/find: opendata_state=NY)

where.description: Conditions on the register's own columns, each "column:op:value" with op eq | starts_with | contains | not_blank, e.g. ["license_status:starts_with:Active"] (/find: opendata_where=)

zips.description: Or cut it to 5-digit ZIP codes, e.g. ["78114", "78154"] (/find: opendata_zips=78114,78154)

b.description: Second set, given the same way

opendata.description: INSTEAD of dataset / datasets / category: a public register read LIVE from its publisher at question time (e.g. a state's licensed child-care programs). Matched by distance only (relate.mode near / not_near, near_m metres). Not a list we sell: the answer names the publisher, licence and read time, and prices only the rows of OUR lists.

radius_miles.description: Distance that counts as together (default 1 mile)
